g.text: Rows: current cells. Columns: next generation. Each row sums to 1; 0 is absorbing.
Numbers that decide the outcome (default parameters)
P(0/2/3) are offspring probabilities without therapy. m = expected offspring = (1−d)(1−k)(2+q); m > 1 grows, m < 1 shrinks.
Therapy (ON) adds extra kill k = 0.90 for sensitive and 0.04 for resistant cells. Resistance is neutral without therapy (same m = 1.428).
Single-cell rules: what one cell does in one generation
Every simulated outcome is built from these per-cell offspring laws
Panels A–B drop mutations, genotype advantages and therapy; the threshold 4 in B is illustrative. Extinct = probability that one cell's lineage eventually dies out (smallest root of s = f(s)).
Starting from 100 baseline cells, total extinction without therapy has probability s^100 ≈ 3e-38.
